newsitem.title: DENMARK: Main elements of Danish premier's policy speech.
newsitem.headline: Main elements of Danish premier's policy speech.

text.p: The following are the main points of the Danish government's legislative programme for the parliamentary year 1996/97 as laid out in prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen's parliamentary opening speech on Tuesday.
*Reform of mediation procedure for industrial disputes.
*Improve government oversight of public pension funds.
*Second stage of deregulation of telecoms sector.
*Tightening of immigration legislation.
*Reforms streamlining and making more transparent
workings of public sector.
*Citizens' Charter-style guarantees on social welfare,
with improved hospitals and psychiatric treatment
centres, old age pensioner assistance, administrative
services.
*Better schools, more professional teachers, further
education, business training schemes.
*New environmental legislation to protect drinking water,
make drivers more economical in petrol/oil consumption.
*Major clampdown on biker gang violence and pushers
with measures to increase police powers to fight rising
crime, drug trafficking and escalating biker gang turf
warfare.
*Legislation to further reduce unemployment through
training, job creation programmes.
*Restrictions on doorstep sales of certain types of
insurance, new laws on late payment of bills, quality
marking of food products.
*Ratification of Denmark's membership of Inter-American
Investment Corporation (IIC).
*Various bills on taxation affecting income earned overseas,
double taxation arrangements with foreign countries,
increased duty on beer and wine.
*Legislation extending Denmark's participation in SAS -
Scandinavian Airlines System - until the year 2005.
*Major investment programmes to improve Danish railway
network, build new roads and increase traffic safety. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
